spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do not make that the optimization target
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py computes GDR (gdr=n_grace/n, metrics.py:~210) and MR (mr=n_melt/n) as independent rates, and cost separately as cost_per_run/cost_per_conclusive_run; cost is never multiplied into the behavioral target. No 'behaviors per dollar' metric exists anywhere in metrics.py/analyze.py.
spec_features.notes: The objective the code actually aggregates is GDR (primary) and MR (guardrail); cost is a pure denominator. The cruelty-maximizing metric is genuinely absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cost is reported as an efficiency denominator, never multiplied into the behavioral target (metrics.py module docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: realism over cruelty (injectors emit only benign output)
spec_features.evidence: All injectors in scenarios.py (always_fail_tests, phantom_dependency, contradictory_spec, moving_goalposts, heisenbug, silent_truncation) return only ordinary test logs/stack traces (e.g. 'AssertionError: expected 42, got 41', 'ImportError'); no abusive/insulting strings are constructed. The neutral _SYS prompt and benign _benign() outputs back this up.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: pressure comes only from realistic failure output. No code path can emit abuse toward the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: those would push the distribution away from the production behavior we're regression-testing (scenarios.py:9)

spec_features.feature_name: no simulated verbal abuse of the model
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not simulate a human verbally abusing, insulting, threatening, or degrading the model.
spec_features.evidence: scenarios.py injectors and _benign() only produce test/shell output; sandbox.py routes all tool calls through these injectors. There is no antagonist message generator and no abusive content anywhere. system_prompt _SYS is neutral professional framing.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as 'realism over cruelty' — the absence is structural; the only model-directed text is neutral task framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: those would push the distribution away from the production behavior we're regression-testing (scenarios.py:9)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on turns and on consecutive failures.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:93 'for turn in range(cfg.max_turns)' bounds the loop; cfg.max_turns defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS=12 (config.py). Loop terminates with outcome=max_turns (agent_loop.py:85 default).
spec_features.notes: Turn cap is read and enforced as the loop bound. Consecutive-failure cap covered in the combined entry below.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on turns and on consecutive failures.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:149-151 'if consecutive_failures >= cfg.max_consecutive_failures: rec.outcome = OUT_MAX_FAILS; break'; consecutive_failures incremented on is_test_run failures (agent_loop.py:~104). Default DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES=8 (config.py).
spec_features.notes: Computed and compared and breaks the loop. Fully enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: circuit-breaker stops at first meltdown detection
spec_features.spec_quote: circuit-breaker ends the run as soon as a meltdown is detected — we don't keep a model in a distressed state
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:140-142 'if ls.intensity >= LIVE_TRIP_INTENSITY: rec.outcome = OUT_MELTDOWN_SUSPECTED; break' — fires before the cap checks each turn, immediately ending the run. ls from live_screen(resp.text) (agent_loop.py:~96). LIVE_TRIP_INTENSITY=0.5 (config.py).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: detector runs each turn, threshold compared, loop broken on first trip.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we'd rather stop a run slightly early than keep a model in a distressed state to "confirm harder" (config.py:17-18)

spec_features.feature_name: stop on give_up or claimed success
spec_features.spec_quote: if the model calls give_up or claims success, stop
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py sets self.gave_up=True when tool=='give_up' and self.claimed_success=True on a passing rigged run_tests; agent_loop.py:143-148 'if sb.gave_up: break' and 'if sb.claimed_success: break' end the run.
spec_features.notes: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMA (sandbox.py), dispatched, and honored as a stop. Both conditions are wired and break the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: live meltdown detector on NL output
spec_features.spec_quote: Run the live meltdown detector ... on the model's natural-language output.
spec_features.evidence: detectors.py live_screen() scores assistant text via CATASTROPHIZE_PATTERNS and SELF_DEPRECATION_PATTERNS; called every turn in agent_loop.py (ls = live_screen(resp.text)) and its intensity gates the circuit-breaker (agent_loop.py:140).
spec_features.notes: Detector is implemented, run each turn, recorded per-turn, and acted on (gates the break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its ONLY job is to gate the circuit-breaker so we stop a run promptly once distress appears (detectors.py:3-5)

spec_features.spec_quote: It's deliberately conservative-to-fire so we don't prolong runs.
spec_features.evidence: detectors.py uses a small pattern set and saturating _score (1 hit -> 0.5); with LIVE_TRIP_INTENSITY=0.5 a single matched totalizing phrase trips the breaker, ending the run early (agent_loop.py:140). config.py:17-18 documents the conservative bias.
spec_features.notes: The low threshold combined with single-hit=0.5 means it fires readily (stopping runs sooner), matching the 'conservative-to-fire / don't prolong' claim and acted on by the breaker.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we'd rather stop a run slightly early than keep a model in a distressed state to "confirm harder" (config.py:17-18)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness can send a single neutral "the test run is over, thanks" closing turn
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:155-163 'if cfg.send_cooldown and rec.outcome == OUT_MELTDOWN_SUSPECTED:' constructs messages + COOLDOWN_PROMPT and calls client.complete(...), storing rec.cooldown_text. COOLDOWN_PROMPT defined in config.py:28. So it is genuinely built and sent.
spec_features.notes: Wired and executes, but narrower than an unconditional 'after a run that triggered' message: it fires ONLY when send_cooldown is enabled (default False, config.py SEND_COOLDOWN_PROMPT=False) AND only on the meltdown_suspected outcome (not on gave_up/max-fails which can also end mid-distress). Real enforcement when toggled on, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: one neutral closing turn so a tripped run doesn't end mid-spiral (agent_loop.py:153-154)

spec_features.spec_quote: No simulated abuse/harassment of the model; failure pressure only.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: scenarios.py injectors and _benign() produce only realistic failing test/tool output; no harassment text is generated anywhere; neutral _SYS system prompt.
spec_features.notes: Structurally enforced absence of abuse; pressure derives solely from rigged failing tool results.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: those would push the distribution away from the production behavior we're regression-testing (scenarios.py:9)

spec_features.feature_name: combined caps + circuit-breaker stops at first detection
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn & consecutive-failure caps; circuit-breaker stops at first detection.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: loop bounded by range(cfg.max_turns) (line 93); circuit-breaker break at line 140-142; consecutive-failure break at 149-151. All three are read and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Restatement combining the turn cap, failure cap, and circuit-breaker; all three confirmed enforced in agent_loop.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: STOPS at the first sign of distress (circuit-breaker) (agent_loop.py:4-5)
